question: What fruit does the practitioner gain from this deity-satisfaction rite?
premises: The rite includes satisfaction of the deity.
That satisfaction rests on the path of both body and vital breath.
The verse compares its result to the fruits of pilgrimages, austerities, sacrifices, gifts, and similar acts.
inference: By satisfying the deity through the path of both body and vital breath, the practitioner obtains the fruit of all pilgrimages, austerities, sacrifices, gifts, and similar meritorious acts.
plain_english: Through satisfaction of the deity, resting on the path of both body and vital breath, one obtains the fruit of all pilgrimages, austerities, sacrifices, gifts, and the like.
